notes.summary: Base-K finite wide-polyannulus Picard vanishing by staged disc/circle gluing; no arbitrary-extension claim.
notes.detailedSummary: Using only Gruson IV.5 for pure discs and unit circles, SK0 cancellation trivializes rank-one projectives. Filling an annular hole along its inner circle reduces the number of wide factors in both the boundary and filled spaces. This proves Pic(P_m,K)=0 for every m over K=C((s)), under the named coherent-affinoid foundations. It is a finite Picard bridge, not the original E1 theorem.
notes.text:
# n1. Filling annular holes closes the finite base-K Picard gate

This is an unverified proof draft, not an execution certificate. Retain K=C((s)) with |s|=exp(-1/8). The result is Pic(P_m,K)=0 for every integer m>=1, where P_m,K is the product of the two closed annuli |s|^m<=|z_j|<=|s|^(-m). In fact the argument proves the following slightly larger finite statement over this same K: every finite product of closed discs, circles, and closed annuli whose positive radii belong to |K*| has zero analytic Picard group. No arbitrary-extension quantifier is needed or claimed.

The source input is precisely Gruson, *Fibres vectoriels sur un polydisque ultrametrique*, Ann. Sci. ENS (4) 1 (1968), 45--89, IV.5, Theorem 1 (printed pp. 79--81). Its H is a completed tensor product of disc algebras T_(1,r), r in Q tensor v(K*), and unit-circle algebras C. The conclusion includes SK^0(H)=0; SK^0 is the cokernel of Z->[K^0(H)] sending 1 to [H]. This theorem concerns discs and circles. It is never applied here with a wide-annulus factor. Its full immediate proof and the K^0 dependencies are recorded in the local source ledger. Only the K^0 conclusion is used, so its additional SK^1 calculation and its valued-excellence dependency are not needed for the inference below.

First, SK^0(H)=0 implies Pic(H)=0. The finite analytic line bundles on an affinoid correspond to finite projective modules of rank one. If P has rank one, its class in K^0(H) is n[H] for an integer n; evaluating rank at any prime gives n=1. Equality in the Grothendieck group of the direct-sum monoid of finite projectives means P direct-sum Q is isomorphic to H direct-sum Q for some finite projective Q. Taking top exterior powers gives P tensor det(Q) isomorphic to det(Q). Tensoring with the dual of det(Q) gives P isomorphic to H. Thus no cancellation assertion for arbitrary vector bundles is required. A circle of radius c in |K*| is carried to a unit circle by z->z/a with |a|=c. Discs are similarly rescaled to unit discs. This proves the zero-Picard assertion for products having no wide-annulus factors.

We use analytic G-sheaves for line bundles. Finite rational-domain covers support sheaf gluing; the affinoid correspondence and coherent descent are the Tate--Kiehl foundations, in the precise formulation of Van der Put, *Rigid analytic spaces* (1975--76), 2.14--2.16.3 and 3.4.5--6. The complete immediate proof of 2.16.3, including its explicit descent diagram, has been read; it cites Kiehl for the deeper affinoid descent theorem. These covers are not represented as ordinary open covers for a psh construction.

Here is the induction, which repairs the foundation without asserting arbitrary-base factoriality. Write D(R)={|z|<=R}, D(r)={|z|<=r}, A(r,R)={r<=|z|<=R}, and C(r)={|z|=r}, with 0<r<R in |K*|. Suppose all finite products with fewer than k wide-annulus factors, and any number of disc or circle factors, have zero Picard group. Let Z=A(r,R) times Y have k such factors. The product D(R) times Y has k-1; the overlap C(r) times Y has k-1 as well.

Take ANY analytic line bundle L on Z. Its restriction to C(r) times Y is trivial by induction. Choose one frame there. On D(r) times Y take the trivial bundle and identify its frame with that chosen frame on the overlap. The two analytic domains A(r,R) times Y and D(r) times Y cover D(R) times Y; they are rational domains, their intersection is exactly C(r) times Y, and they form a finite admissible affinoid cover. For example, the two inequalities |z/a|<=1 and |a/z|<=1, with |a|=r, give the disc and annular sides; the denominator z together with the nonzero constant a generates the unit ideal. Their products with Y remain rational domains. The chosen isomorphism and its inverse give descent data; the two-member cocycle condition is automatic. Ordinary sheaf gluing on this analytic G-cover produces an invertible sheaf L' on D(R) times Y. Local freeness and coherence descend by the stated affinoid theorem. By induction L' is trivial, so its restriction L is trivial. This proves the induction for every k.

For the exact two-variable case one may check the order without any induction shorthand. First prove Pic(C_1 times A_2)=0 by extending across the second hole: the overlap C_1 times C_2 and the filled space C_1 times D_2 are pure circle/disc products. Next extend an arbitrary L on A_1 times A_2 to D_1 times A_2 using that boundary result. Finally extend to D_1 times D_2 using the pure product D_1 times C_2 on the second overlap. The bidisc is covered by Gruson. In particular, the delicate intermediate D_1 times A_2 is proved by filling, not by applying his theorem to a wide-annulus base.

Taking r=|s|^m, R=|s|^(-m) establishes the exact base-field gate F_K for every m. No topological contractibility argument, formal-model extension assertion, pro-homotopy limit, or regular-factorial-base restricted-variable theorem is used. This is a complete finite Picard bridge under the stated standard affinoid foundations, not the original finite-energy equation. It makes no assertion about arbitrary radii outside |K*| or arbitrary complete extensions L/K.

notes.summary: Base-field nonalgebraization of the explicit proper analytic surface, excluding all separated finite-type algebraic spaces.
notes.detailedSummary: The Picard bridge from n1 gives compatible global torus frames. Inner Gauss bounds, the signed coefficient recurrence and every meromorphic pole divisor yield Gamma(X,M)=K for periods (s^8,2),(3,s^8). Smoothness reflection, generic-field hypotheses and analytic divisor descent exclude all separated finite-type K-algebraic-space algebraizations. Exact deeper analytic foundations remain cited; no arbitrary-extension scope or full equation theory is claimed.
notes.text:
# n2. Base-field nonalgebraization via compatible frames and all pole divisors

Retain K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8. Let T=(G_m^2)^an, lambda_1=(t,2), lambda_2=(3,t), Lambda=<lambda_1,lambda_2>, and X=T/Lambda. With the finite Picard bridge n1, the following argument no longer assumes F_K. It excludes EVERY separated finite-type K-algebraic space algebraization of X, not just projective schemes or algebraic group uniformizations. This is an unverified mathematical draft using the explicitly named analytic foundations; it does not solve P16.7.

Write x=(-log|z_1|,-log|z_2|). Multiplication by lambda(n)=lambda_1^(n_1)lambda_2^(n_2) sends x to x+n. Inverse images of open rectangles of widths less than one have disjoint nonidentity deck translates. Their quotient maps are ordinary open analytic charts, glued by locally constant deck transformations satisfying the cocycle. This constructs X. The applied open-quotient gluing statement and its entire immediate proof are Conrad--Temkin, *Non-archimedean analytification of algebraic spaces*, author version dated 24 February 2009, Lemma 4.2.3. The action relation in T times_K T is a locally finite union of closed translation graphs: on any pair of relatively compact subsets of T only finitely many n can occur, since n lies in a bounded difference of tropical-coordinate ranges. Thus its map to T times_K T is a closed immersion. Closed diagonals descend through the local isomorphism atlas; Conrad--Temkin 4.2.4 and its adjacent closed-immersion descent proof justify this in the analytic category, beyond mere Hausdorffness. X is separated.

The compact strict polyannulus x^(-1)([0,1]^2) surjects onto X. Goodness and strictness can also be seen pointwise: choose a center in (1/8 Z)^2 within 1/16 in each coordinate of a lift; the closed rectangle of width 1/2 about it lies in the open rectangle of width 3/4, which is a quotient chart. Its inverse image is a strict affinoid neighborhood of the point. Local charts are ordinary opens of the smooth boundaryless torus. Consequently X is good, strict, smooth, of pure dimension two, boundaryless and compact; with separatedness these are precisely analytic properness. T is connected: its nested centered closed polyannuli have integral Laurent algebras and nonempty intersections. Hence X is connected. Only this base-K geometry is asserted here.

We first prove Pic(T)=0, including compatibility along the noncompact exhaustion. Put a=1/8 and P_m={|s|^m<=|z_i|<=|s|^(-m)}. By n1 choose a frame e_m of a given line bundle on P_m. Every unit f on P_m has an inner estimate as follows. Its convergent Laurent expansion is sum b_beta z^beta. At the Gauss seminorm of log-radii y in [-ma,ma]^2, log|f| is the maximum of log|b_beta|+beta dot y. It and the corresponding function for f^(-1) are convex and sum to zero, so both are affine. A term achieving the maximum at an interior point has an integral slope alpha; since an affine function nonnegative on a neighborhood and zero at an interior point has zero linear part, that term agrees with the maximum affine function. The vertex inequalities yield

|b_beta/b_alpha| exp(ma |beta-alpha|_1)<=1.

It follows that f=b_alpha z^alpha(1+g), with zero constant coefficient in g and ||g||_(P_j)<=|s|^(m-j) for j<m. On P_m itself 1+g is a unit; no strict boundary estimate is claimed. For a unit on all of T the same affine Gauss-norm argument on all of R^2 makes it exactly b z^alpha, since any distinct exponent would dominate on some ray.

Choose frames successively and divide the (m+1)-st by a global scalar monomial to arrange e_(m+1)|_(P_m)=(1+g_m)e_m. For fixed j, the products p_j=product_(m=j)^infinity(1+g_m)|_(P_j) converge to units: the first factor is a unit, while all later errors have norm at most |s|^(m-j) tending to zero. Their inverse products also converge by the geometric series for the tail factors. The frames E_j=e_j p_j satisfy E_(j+1)|_(P_j)=E_j. Because P_j lies in the interior of P_(j+1), this exhaustion is admissible, and the frames glue to a frame on T. This proves Pic(T)=0 rather than simply choosing unrelated finite frames.

Pull any line bundle on X to T and use this global frame. A global section becomes an analytic Laurent function f satisfying

f(lambda z)=c_lambda z^(h_lambda) f(z),

where each multiplier is a global unit, hence a scalar monomial. Commuting the two deck transformations gives lambda_1^(h_2)=lambda_2^(h_1). Write h_1=(A,B), h_2=(C,D); the equality is t^C 2^D=3^A t^B. Valuations give C=B; then prime valuations in Q* give A=D=0. Thus h_1=(0,k), h_2=(k,0). The exponent map is additive on Lambda.

If k!=0 take n=(1,sign(k)), lambda=lambda(n), h=(k n_2,k n_1). Then h!=0 and Q=v(lambda^h)=2|k|>0. Comparing Laurent coefficients in f(lambda z)=c z^h f(z), starting with a_m!=0, gives for integers j>=0

a_(m+jh)=a_m c^j lambda^(-jm-hj(j+1)/2).

Its valuation has quadratic leading term -Q j(j+1)/2, and therefore tends to -infinity. On the fixed unit polyannulus the Laurent coefficients must tend to zero as their exponents escape to infinity, a contradiction. If k=0, two nonzero coefficients at exponents m,m' would give lambda_i^(m-m')=1 for both i. The valuations are respectively m_1-m'_1 and m_2-m'_2, so m=m'. Thus every nonzero section in this situation is a scalar monomial and is nowhere zero.

For an arbitrary nonzero meromorphic F on X, pull back to T. Smooth affinoid algebras are noetherian regular rings. The exact commutative algebra inputs are: every regular local ring is a UFD (current Stacks 0AG0, full statement and immediate inductive proof freshly read), and every noetherian normal domain R equals the intersection of R_p over its height-one primes inside its fraction field (031T, full statement and immediate proof freshly read). Define the pole module on a fraction chart as J={a in O:aF in O}. It is coherent as the kernel of the multiplication map to the denominator quotient. Localization at each prime of its regular affinoid algebra makes this ideal principal by unique factorization, with precisely the nonnegative pole orders. Thus it is a finite locally free rank-one module. These modules agree on overlaps by their intrinsic definition, giving the invertible subsheaf O(-P) of O. This constructs the effective Cartier pole divisor for all local meromorphic fractions, rather than just selected characters. Analytic sheaf restriction and affinoid coherent descent are the named Tate--Kiehl foundations. In particular, this step does not assert that an arbitrary analytic meromorphic sheaf follows from a fraction equalizer.

Trivialize O(-P)=J on T using Pic(T)=0, obtaining an analytic function f_0 with divisor P. Since f_0 is a section of the intrinsic pole ideal J, f_1=F f_0 is analytic by the DEFINITION of J, without assuming every meromorphic sheaf section is already one global affinoid fraction. Equivalently, on each local fraction chart the noetherian normal-domain intersection theorem removes all height-one poles. At a pole the numerator f_1 has order zero, and elsewhere f_0 has order zero, so they have no common height-one divisor. Lambda-invariance of F identifies the translated pole ideal with J. Its two global frames therefore differ by an analytic unit: f_0(lambda z)/f_0(z) and its inverse are analytic. The normal height-one criterion checks the same fact on fraction charts. Both f_0 and f_1 have the same scalar-monomial multipliers. The preceding recurrence forces k=0 and both functions to be scalar multiples of the same monomial. Therefore Gamma(X,M)=K. This argument includes all meromorphic pole divisors.

Now suppose Y is a separated finite-type K-algebraic space and Y^an is isomorphic to X. Conrad--Temkin 2.3.1, with its full immediate proof, reflects smoothness; Example 2.3.2 compares closed-point residue fields and completed local rings. The Berkovich/rigid dictionary applies because X is strict, good, separated and compact. Thus Y is smooth of dimension two. A nontrivial clopen decomposition would analytify to one, and every nonempty finite-type piece has a closed point with nonempty analytification, so Y is connected. Its finitely many irreducible components are disjoint and open by regularity. Hence Y is integral.

Here are the exact algebraic-space hypotheses. Regular noetherian etale charts have no embedded associated primes, so their weakly associated points are minimal. Finite-type charts satisfy all four equivalent finite-component conditions of Stacks 0BB1. Separatedness implies decency and field monomorphisms representing generic points. Stacks 086U gives a dense open scheme locus; for integral Y it contains the unique generic point. Stacks 0ENA, whose three hypotheses are just checked, identifies its global algebraic meromorphic functions with rational functions; 0END identifies this ring with the generic field K(Y). Stacks 0EN6 supplies the total-fraction description on affine etale charts. The current complete statements and immediate proofs were freshly read. A dense affine schematic open and Noether normalization give trdeg_K K(Y)=2.

We must separately construct the analytic meromorphic image. On regular Y a rational function has a Cartier pole divisor, an associated invertible sheaf, and numerator and denominator regular sections, all descending algebraically through etale charts. Analytify the sheaf and the sections using the coherent analytification functor of Conrad--Temkin 2.3. On scheme charts the local map from an algebraic local ring to the analytic local ring is flat: Ducros, *Families of Berkovich spaces*, 2.1.4 states regularity for schemes locally of finite type over an affinoid algebra, citing Berkovich 1993 Proposition 2.6.2 for flatness and Ducros 2009 Theorem 3.3 for regularity. Those deeper theorems are cited foundations, not immediate proofs supplied in this memoir. A local flat map is faithfully flat and preserves nonzerodivisors. Hence the ratio of the analytified sections is analytic meromorphic; that property descends across the analytic etale charts. To see injectivity choose a closed point of a dense affine scheme open outside the zeros of a nonzero numerator and denominator. Its finite residue extension of K is complete, and its analytic point has nonzero fraction value. We obtain a K-embedding K(Y)->Gamma(X,M)=K, contradicting transcendence degree two.

This excludes all separated finite-type algebraic spaces over the retained K. No arbitrary-extension nonalgebraization is claimed. The explicit real analytic positivity datum for future equation work is theta=d'd''((x_1^2+x_2^2)/2); the change under x->x+n is n dot x+|n|^2/2 with zero Hessian. No ample algebraic line bundle is introduced. Nonalgebraization supplies a foundation for P16.7, but the unbounded all-direction finite-energy operator and every-admissible-measure existence and uniqueness still remain unproved.

Artifacts: notes/n2.md, P16.7-standalone-paper.tex, proof-companion.md, source-application-ledger.md. Own recurrence diagnostics are rerun with `python scripts/diagnostics.py`; they do not prove infinite Laurent convergence or algebraic-space descent. Support: n1 only.

notes.summary: New constant-energy branch pencils defeat uniform energy-bounded compactness and force a quantitative finite-dual branch-tail bound.
notes.detailedSummary: The ordinary bounded middle-positive class C_theta has genuine mixed measures of raw mass two. For every real N>=1, U_N has mass-one delta_xi_N off the original Gauss section and energy -1/6-N/3. The pencil u0+aD_N has E=-1/6-a^3 N/3 and MA=(1-a^2)MA(u0)+a^2 MA(U_N). Choosing a=N^(-1/3) gives normalized E=-2/3 and rigid value -1/4-N^(2/3), disproving uniform compactness on this energy-bounded set. Finite bounded dual energy implies mu(B_N)<=constant*N^(-2/3). These are necessary constraints, not unbounded E1 or an admissible counterexample.
notes.text:
# n3. Ordinary bounded products and a constant-energy branch obstruction

Use the actual base-K quotient X of n2, with K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8 and periods (t,2),(3,t). No supplied note is a premise. This note constructs its bounded ordinary-local operator anew, verifies the checkpoint for EVERY real N>=1, and proves two new consequences: normalized constant-energy potentials fail uniform compactness, and finite bounded dual energy imposes a quantitative branch-tail condition. Neither conclusion is a counterexample to the literal P16.7 equation.

Let DD=d'd''. On a deck sheet put x_j=-log|z_j|, q=|x|^2/2 and theta=DDq. Under x->x+n the potential changes by n dot x+|n|^2/2, a smooth DD-null function, so theta is a global real analytic datum. Define C_theta to consist of continuous real u for which q+u is locally on ORDINARY opens a locally uniform limit of ordinary CLD smooth functions having positive semidefinite Hessian. This is an explicit bounded generated class, without recognition of any larger psh class.

We first justify the bounded calculus rather than importing it. In an m-dimensional moment presentation, symmetric (p,p) coefficients, with the usual sign, are symmetric matrices on Lambda^p R^m. Their dimension is d(d+1)/2, d=binomial(m,p). Middle positivity is the PSD cone. For m=4,p=2, d=6 and the coefficient space has dimension 21. Strong squares ww^t satisfy Q(w)=w12 w34-w13 w24+w14 w23=0. Their span has dimension EXACTLY 20: Q=0 characterizes decomposable bivectors, by expressing a bivector with a nonzero coefficient as a wedge of two vectors (equivalently its skew matrix has rank two). With x=(w12,w13,w14), y=(w34,-w24,w23), Q=x dot y. A quadratic form R vanishing for x dot y=0 has no pure-x or pure-y part, by setting the other variable zero. Write its remaining part x^t B y. For each x, vanishing for every y perpendicular to x makes B^t x a multiple of x; testing basis vectors and their pairwise sums makes B scalar. Hence the annihilator is precisely the one-dimensional span of Q. In particular (e12+e34)(e12+e34)^t has Q=1 and is outside that span. Strong squares supply NO ambient order unit in this presentation.

The middle cone supplies the needed order unit. If lambda is the Euclidean positive (1,1) form, lambda^p has coefficient matrix p! I. Every symmetric smooth coefficient matrix B on a compact tropical support satisfies -C lambda^p<=B<=C lambda^p. A nonnegative smooth cutoff, equal to one on that support and compactly supported in the same ordinary open, decomposes the test form into two middle-positive compactly supported forms. Local moment representations, a finite cover of its compact support, and a smooth partition of unity globalize this. The positive supports may grow but stay compact inside the specified open. CLD-v2 1.2.6-13 and 6.5.1-3 state the middle-cone and decomposition results; 15.1.1 and 15.2.3-9 supply ordinary moment charts, cutoffs and density on locally holomorphically separated spaces. X satisfies these hypotheses because it is good, separated and boundaryless. The directly applied statements and immediate proofs are recorded locally; no strong-domination assertion from 7.2.9 is used.

For a symmetric middle-positive current T and a positive test eta, the functional phi-><T,phi eta> is positive. A cutoff plateau bounds it by ||phi||_infinity times <T,chi eta> on compact sets. Smooth scalar density and Riesz give a Radon measure. If beta=eta_+-eta_-, subtract the two scalar measures. Equality on smooth scalars proves independence of the decomposition and support in supp(beta); antisymmetric tests pair to zero. Continuous multiplication is thereby defined and obeys

|<bT,beta>| <= sup_K|b| <T,eta_++eta_->,

where K is the compact union of their supports. If positive T_j->T weakly and b_j->b locally uniformly, approximate b on K by a smooth g within epsilon. Split b_j T_j-bT into (b_j-g)T_j+g(T_j-T)+(g-b)T. The first and last terms are bounded by the displayed inequality, with a bounded sequence <T_j,eta_++eta_->; the middle term tends to zero. Let epsilon tend to zero. This proves multiplication continuity on the fixed bounded class. These are the exact scalar and coefficient-measure arguments of CLD-v2 7.2.8 and 7.2.11-12, here reconstructed with the middle order unit.

For closed symmetric T and smooth h, the complementary-degree Leibniz rule gives DD(hT)=DDh wedge T. Arbitrary continuous multipliers need not preserve closedness. For u,v in C_theta define alpha_u=theta+DD[u] and, locally with f=q+u,g=q+v,

B(u,v)=DD(f DD[g]).

Smooth-positive approximants give DDg_j->DDg; multiplication continuity gives f_j DDg_j->f DDg. Differentiating identifies B as the limit of the positive smooth mixed products, independently of the approximants. It is symmetric and positive, and the smooth DD-null change rule glues it on ordinary overlaps. Differences of such potentials inherit bilinearity by subtraction. No arbitrary-current density or upward recognition is asserted. The applied bounded recursive units are CLD-v2 8.5.1, 8.5.3, 8.5.5, 8.7.1-4 and 8.8.1, 8.8.4-8. The overbroad continuous-multiplier closedness in 8.6.7 is unnecessary.

Canonical integration of CLD-v2 14.3.1-5 and 14.5.2-3 retains all generic Artinian lengths and calibration degrees. CLD-v2 15.7.1-2 gives the canonical tropical level equal to pure analytic dimension on a topologically separated analytic space, with its analytic boundary. Thus this positive top current on the boundaryless surface is an actual analytic Radon measure. These deep analytic integration foundations are cited; their full dependency trees are not newly proved. The identity torus moment and translated identity moments used below have saturated lattice Z^2 and actual degree one. The exterior-product factor is 2!, so theta^2=2 i_*dx, with dx probability Haar measure on R^2/Z^2, and the RAW reference mass is two. It cannot be replaced silently by probability mass.

Globally B(u,v)=theta wedge alpha_v+DD(u alpha_v), and theta wedge alpha_v=theta^2+DD(v theta). Pairing the differentiated terms with 1 on compact boundaryless X makes them zero. Hence every B(u,v) has mass two. Define MA_theta(u)=B(u,u). The multiplication argument proves uniform continuity within C_theta. Dini only gives decreasing continuity when the limit is still continuous and in this class. Convex nondecreasing regularizations of max preserve Hessian positivity by the smooth chain rule, so C_theta is convex and closed under finite maxima. With w=max(u,v-epsilon), ordinary locality on its two strict regions and equal mass give

MA_theta(v){u<v-epsilon} <= 2-MA_theta(u){u>v-epsilon}=MA_theta(u){u<=v-epsilon}.

As epsilon decreases to zero both sets on the sides increase to {u<v}. This proves bounded comparison, without full-E1 comparison or uniqueness.

Let G(y)=y^2/2-y/2+1/12 on [0,1], periodically extended. Its mean is zero, G''=dy-delta_0, and u0=-G(x1)-G(x2) has range [-1/6,1/12]. Nonnegative periodic convolutions give smooth-positive approximants to q+u0. Their diagonal squares and the continuity just proved give

A=alpha_u0, MA_theta(u0)=A^2=2 delta_i(0),
theta wedge A=i_*(dy tensor delta_0+delta_0 tensor dy).

The entire fibre F=tau^-1(0) has u0=-1/6. Choose its ordinary sheet V={|x_j|<1/4}. For EVERY real N>=1 put r=exp(-N), ell_j=log max(r,|z_j-1|), b_j=log max(1,|z_j|), d_j=ell_j-b_j and D_N=max(d1,d2). Real constants in convex functions and Gauss seminorms permit these radii even when r is outside |K*|; no new strict-affinoid assertion for radius r is needed. Each d_j<=0 and is zero if |z_j|!=1. Thus D_N is zero off F and extends continuously by zero outside V. Its negative locus

W={|z1-1|<1, |z2-1|<1}

is ORDINARY open, contained in F. On V one directly computes

q+U_N=max(ell1+b2,b1+ell2)-(1/2)log|z1 z2|-1/6, U_N=u0+D_N.

Every ell_j is constant near a zero of z_j-1; omit that inactive coordinate on that neighborhood. Elsewhere the analytic functions involved are invertible and their logarithms define ordinary moment charts. Sums and maxima in the display are convex functions of those logarithms, and the last logarithm is smooth pluriharmonic. Softmax or convolution supplies actual ordinary smooth-positive approximants. No logarithmic chart crosses a zero. This proves U_N in the EXACT C_theta, not an unspecified current-defined or generated larger class.

In W write w_j=z_j-1. The local weight is log max(r,|w1|,|w2|)-1/6. The bidisc Gauss seminorm xi_N with both w-radii r is an actual analytic point of W, where |z_j-1|=r<1. At the original Gauss point i(0) these values are one, so xi_N is off that section. Near xi_N, w1,w2 are invertible and the translated identity moment has lattice Z^2 and degree one. With y_j=log|w_j|+N, regularize max(0,y1,y2) by epsilon log(1+exp(y1/epsilon)+exp(y2/epsilon)). Its gradient is a diffeomorphism onto the interior of the triangle {p_j>0,p1+p2<1}; hence integral det(Hess)=1/2 by change of variables. Rescaling y=epsilon Y gives concentration at zero. The calibrated exterior square multiplies by 2!, giving mass one. Its smooth measures live on the translated Gauss section by CLD-v2 5.8.1-6; its continuity, established by direct evaluation of Gauss seminorms (12.1.2-5), gives convergence against continuous ANALYTIC tests. Operator continuity identifies the analytic atom. At every other point of the invertible-w chart the weight is locally affine or, after subtracting an affine function, depends on a single coordinate, so its square is zero. Near w_j=0 omit the inactive log, again giving rank at most one. Therefore MA_theta(U_N)|W=delta_xi_N. Its total mass is two. The remaining mass one outside W is deliberately NOT identified.

On W, q and u0 are constant, so theta|W=A|W=0. The scalar D_N is zero on its complement, including its boundary. The coefficient-measure calculus gives D_N theta=D_N A=0 globally by ordinary locality, not a nonsmooth integration-by-parts assertion. Therefore theta wedge alpha_U_N=theta wedge A. Outside F, U_N=u0 on ordinary neighborhoods, so MA_theta(U_N) is supported on F. Also D_N vanishes everywhere on the original Gauss section. The complete three-term energy is

E_theta(u)=(1/3) integral u(theta^2+theta wedge alpha_u+MA_theta(u)),
integral U_N theta^2=0,
integral U_N(theta wedge alpha_U_N)=-1/6,
integral U_N MA_theta(U_N)=-1/3-N,
E_theta(U_N)=-1/6-N/3.

At the rigid point y=(1,1), U_N(y)=-1/6-N and E_theta(U_N)-2U_N(y)=1/6+5N/3. Thus E*_C_theta(2 delta_y)=infinity. For comparison, circle potentials with dy+h''>=0 are h=-G*nu+c; their energy is e(h)=integral h dy-(1/2) integral |h'|^2 dy. Convolution proves integral h d(dy+h'')=integral h dy-integral |h'|^2 and e(k)-e(h)=integral(k-h)d(dy+h'')-(1/2) integral|k'-h'|^2. For separable sums their bounded mixed energy is 2(e(h1)+e(h2)). The rigid mass-two objective only sees the two delta_0 marginals, is maximized at u0, and equals -1/6-2(-1/6)=1/6. This restricted dual does not supply full admissibility. Any extension inherits the infinite rigid dual ONLY after verifying containment of C_theta and identity of bounded energy.

Here is the new energy-bounded obstruction. For 0<=a<=1 let V_(a,N)=u0+aD_N=(1-a)u0+aU_N, which belongs to C_theta. Bilinearity for differences gives A wedge DD D_N=DD(D_N A)=0. Expanding alpha_V^2 therefore yields

MA_theta(V_(a,N))=(1-a^2)MA_theta(u0)+a^2 MA_theta(U_N),
theta wedge alpha_V=theta wedge A.

Both terms on the right are actual bounded measures. Their support is F, where u0=-1/6; D_N vanishes at i(0), and its integral against MA_theta(U_N) is -N. Hence the three energy integrals are 0, -1/6, and -1/3-a^3 N. Consequently

E_theta(V_(a,N))=-1/6-a^3 N/3,
V_(a,N)(y)=-1/6-aN,
sup V_(a,N)=1/12.

The last equality follows because D_N<=0 and a maximum of u0 lies outside F. Along this entire admissible pencil dE/da=-a^2 N=integral D_N MA_theta(V_(a,N)); this is a verified pencil first variation, not all-direction variation.

Choose a=N^(-1/3). Then E_theta(V_(a,N))=-1/2 for all real N>=1, while V_(a,N)(y)=-1/6-N^(2/3). Subtracting the supremum gives sup v_N=0, E_theta(v_N)=-2/3 and v_N(y)=-1/4-N^(2/3). A uniformly relatively compact set of continuous functions on compact X is uniformly bounded, so this normalized, energy-bounded family is NOT uniformly relatively compact. This improves the unscaled U_N test, whose energies tend to minus infinity. It disproves only uniform compactness in this explicit bounded class. It does not disprove compactness in a useful weaker topology, construct an unbounded E1 element, or prove any unbounded continuity theorem. All these v_N have the same Gauss-skeleton restriction; theta-reference L1 alone therefore cannot separate this family, even under the energy bound.

There is also a new necessary measure condition. For a positive Radon mu of RAW mass two, set M=E*_C_theta(mu) and assume M finite. Put J0=E_theta(u0)-integral u0 dmu and C=M-J0>=0. For L_N=integral(-D_N)dmu, testing V_(a,N) gives

a L_N-a^3 N/3<=C for EVERY a in [0,1].

If N>3C/2 and L_N>N, choosing a=1 contradicts this inequality. Thus L_N<=N. If L_N>0 its maximizing a is sqrt(L_N/N), and the optimized inequality is (2/3)L_N^(3/2)/sqrt(N)<=C. Therefore

L_N <= (3C/2)^(2/3) N^(1/3),
mu(B_N) <= (3C/2)^(2/3) N^(-2/3), N>=1 and N>3C/2,
B_N={|z1-1|<=exp(-N), |z2-1|<=exp(-N)}.

Indeed -D_N=N on this closed branch bidisc. For C=0 the inequalities force L_N=0. The bidiscs decrease to y, so continuity from above also gives mu({y})=0. This is a necessary condition, not a sufficient finite-energy characterization or an existence theorem. It is an all-analytic-support test at this specified branch; the skeletal marginal condition alone misses it.

# n4. Full reconstruction of the restricted circle theory and its exact limits

Use X of n2 and the bounded operator of n3. Let C=R/Z with probability Lebesgue dy, and H={h continuous on C: rho_h=dy+h'' is a positive distribution}. Testing against one gives mass one. The kernel G(y)=y^2/2-y/2+1/12 on [0,1], periodically extended, has mean zero and G''=dy-delta_0: its endpoint derivative drops by one. For every circle probability nu put h_nu=-G*nu. Then rho_h_nu=nu. Conversely h-h_rho_h has zero second derivative; as a periodic distribution it is constant. Since G has range [-1/24,1/12] and Lipschitz constant 1/2, the mean-zero potentials have range [-1/12,1/24], Lipschitz constant 1/2 and oscillation at most 1/8. Sup-zero normalization gives a uniformly bounded equicontinuous closed family, hence uniform compactness by Arzela-Ascoli. Distributional positivity passes under uniform limits. These are circle-direction statements only.

Let S_theta={h1(tau1)+h2(tau2): h_j in H}. Positive periodic convolution gives actual ordinary smooth-positive approximants; thus S_theta is contained in C_theta. For u=h1+h2 and v=k1+k2, diagonal smooth Hessians and n3's bounded continuity give the exact ANALYTIC measure equalities

B(u,v)=i_*(rho_h1 tensor rho_k2+rho_k1 tensor rho_h2),
MA_theta(u)=2 i_*(rho_h1 tensor rho_h2).

Product probability convergence follows first on product continuous tests and then on all continuous tests by Stone-Weierstrass. Continuity of the actual Gauss section gives analytic weak convergence. Every measure 2 i_*(nu1 tensor nu2) has the displayed solution h_nu1+h_nu2. Taking marginals recovers each nu_j; circle uniqueness proves uniqueness modulo constants WITHIN S_theta only. X itself is not asserted to split as a product of curves.

All h are Lipschitz, so e(h)=integral h dy-(1/2) integral |h'|^2 dy is finite. Periodic convolution gives uniform convergence of h and L2 convergence of derivatives, while rho_h converges weakly. This proves integral h d rho_h=integral h dy-integral|h'|^2 and

e(k)-e(h)=integral(k-h)d rho_h-(1/2) integral|k'-h'|^2.

Thus e is concave and strictly concave modulo constants, with derivative on every admissible circle segment equal to integration against its curvature. E_sep(u)=2(e(h1)+e(h2)) is independent of the decomposition, since shifting a constant between factors cancels. It satisfies E_sep(u+c)=E_sep(u)+2c. The three analytic measures in n3's mixed energy give respectively 2 sum integral h_j dy, sum(integral h_j dy+integral h_j d rho_hj), and 2 sum integral h_j d rho_hj. Their average is E_sep. This reconstructs the energy normalization without assuming all-direction energy variation.

For ANY positive analytic Radon mu of RAW mass two define E*_sep(mu)=sup over S_theta of (E_sep(u)-integral u dmu). Normalize each factor by sup h_j=0. Then -1/4<=u<=0 and E_sep(u)<=0, while u=0 is allowed; hence 0<=E*_sep(mu)<=1/2. Let nu_j=(tau_j)_*mu/2. The objective is 2 sum(e(h_j)-integral h_j dnu_j). The energy difference identity proves that its maximizer has rho_hj=nu_j, uniquely modulo constants. Its actual MA is their skeletal product 2 i_*(nu1 tensor nu2), regardless of mu's support or correlations. This proves that restricted finiteness is not the original measure criterion. At y=(1,1) the objective equals 1/6 at u0, although its MA is 2 delta_i(0) rather than 2 delta_y. The stronger dual infinity and branch-tail condition are proved in n3, not inferred from this restricted inverse construction.

For completeness, all circle obstacle and variation claims are also reconstructed. For continuous a:C->R let P(a)=sup{h in H:h<=a}. Constants below min a give a nonempty family. Its common Lipschitz bound, its upper bound a, and its constant lower bound give a finite continuous Lipschitz supremum. On R, y^2/2+P(a)(y) is the supremum of convex functions, so is convex. Thus P(a) belongs to H and is the largest admissible minorant. Monotonicity and addition of constants give ||P(a)-P(b)||_infinity<=||a-b||_infinity.

Put p=P(a), F(y)=y^2/2+p(y). If its curvature charged a noncontact arc, select a short interval [c,d] compactly in that arc with positive curvature in its interior. The clearance a-p has a positive minimum there. Replace F on that interval by its endpoint chord. The chord raises F somewhere; its slope lies between the outer one-sided slopes, so the result remains convex. On a fixed compact arc these slopes are bounded, and the increase is at most a constant times d-c. Choose the interval short enough to stay below the obstacle. Repeat the change on integer translates, using F(y+n)=F(y)+ny+n^2/2; the affine correction preserves the chord construction and the periodicity of F-y^2/2. This gives a strictly larger admissible minorant, contradiction. Any positive curvature on an arc can be localized on arbitrarily short such intervals. Hence rho_p is supported on {p=a} and integral(a-p)d rho_p=0.

For continuous v let p_b=P(a+bv). The energy difference identity, its reverse, and the two contact statements give

b integral v d rho_pb <= e(p_b)-e(p) <= b integral v d rho_p.

Nonexpansiveness implies p_b->p uniformly as b->0. Distributional testing and fixed mass imply rho_pb->rho_p weakly. Divide the inequalities by b, reversing them if b<0, to obtain d/db at zero e(P(a+bv))=integral v d rho_p. This supplies orthogonality and first variation in EVERY circle direction; it is not an envelope theorem for arbitrary analytic obstacles, even when the given obstacle happens to be separable.

The full intrinsic E1 attempt has concrete constraints rather than a transferred theorem. C_theta is explicit and admits all the branch pencils of n3 on an actually nonalgebraizable base-K example. Its raw mass and bounded products are fixed. Defining a larger class merely by decreasing limits is insufficient: a pointwise limit outside the established continuous class has no operator here. The uniform compactness route fails on the constant-energy normalized branch family. Skeleton L1 alone identifies distinct bounded potentials and therefore is not a separated topology. The finite dual criterion over a candidate full class must at least imply the branch-tail inequalities after a rigorous containment and energy comparison. These observations leave open whether an appropriate capacity or weak analytic topology has normalized energy-bounded compactness; whether all-direction envelopes stay in a defined psh cone and satisfy orthogonality; and whether full-mass unbounded products, decreasing continuity, first variation, existence for EVERY finite-energy mass-two analytic measure, and uniqueness modulo constants can be proved. No alternative inverse measure is called MA.
